blindSummary: This is a self-governing overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state; same-sex marriage is legal since 2017; the community is tiny, close-knit and low-crime; unlike the administering state, no bathroom-use restriction machinery applies here.
blindOutOfScope: Constitutional status is noted in the summary; general risk guidance follows the administering state.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Sept 2008): a fellow overseas territory of the same administering state defined marriage as between a man and woman amid fears the metropolitan government would impose civil partnerships across its remaining territories (including this one) - context of metropole-territory LGBT-law dynamics.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (April 2017): this territory legalised same-sex marriage and civil partnerships (7-1 vote) after a public consultation found 90% support for same-sex marriage and 94% for civil partnerships - 'an open, tolerant and respectful community'.

Personal blog (June 2017): confirmation from the territory's registrar general that the same-sex marriage bill received royal assent and is law; also confirms same-sex marriage is NOT legal in a nearby dependent territory of the same administering state.

Explainer-site summary of LGBTQ rights in this territory: legal since 1989, equal age of consent since 2005, marriage and civil partnerships since April 2017, stepchild and joint adoption since 2017, constitutional ban on sexual-orientation discrimination, largely positive attitudes (90% consultation support), first Pride event in the capital April 2017.
